cross_response_observations: Multiple responses exhibit fundamental misunderstandings of impartial game theory concepts. Response A and G both produce incorrect period-2 PNPN patterns, with A using arbitrary alternation logic and G incorrectly applying Nim XOR theory to a single-pile subtraction game. Move set errors are prevalent: B excludes 1 treating 2^0 as empty, while F expands the move set to all integers by misinterpreting powers of two as all summable combinations. Convention errors appear in C and D where P/N labels are inverted either globally or at base case, though C does not actually invoke misère play rules. Response E demonstrates a common advanced student error of computing Sprague-Grundy values instead of direct P/N positions, also producing truncated output. Response H fails to terminate entirely, looping on base case analysis. Notably, no response correctly identifies the period-3 PNN pattern arising from the move set {1,2,4,8,16,32,64}. The responses show confusion between different game types (subtraction games vs Nim), improper base case handling, and overcomplication through unnecessary mathematical machinery.
